baseline: Current coordinator worktree, 2026-11-20; Linux x86_64, Python 3.14, PyTorch 2.15.
implementation: Added focused runtime checks proving that only explicit Provider layer_edit claims can become activation-eligible, only for the tested payload and disposable fixture expectations.

A missing fixture assertion keeps coverage partial; an untested additional declared capability also keeps coverage partial and blocks activation. Unsupported capability declarations are reported as skipped, while conditional claims remain non-activating.

Verification evidence returned by a successful supported check binds the exact payload digest, conformance suite version, Provider and fixture source fingerprints, Python version, and PyTorch version. The existing application layer records the manifest digest alongside that evidence and runtime references re-check it before executing edits.

Added an independent CLI acceptance entry point that exercises the existing separately packaged Provider workflow, fixture assertions, undo/redo, export restore, and tamper rejection without adding a CLI-specific extension implementation.

Provider activation evidence now fingerprints Provider/fixture source before fixture execution and compares it again after the assertions. If either source changes during the conformance run, coverage is downgraded to partial and no executable verification evidence is emitted.

Added an independent capability-driven conformance helper for custom transforms already executable through data.transforms.run_transform_pipeline. It executes a module:callable transform against a fresh fixture, checks the declared output port contract and finite tensor output, distinguishes supported/conditional/unsupported claims, and verifies actual transformed values in an integration test. This does not register a new extension manifest kind or add CLI component-test dispatch.

Integrated registered transform conformance into the real component discover/test CLI path. Rust validates schema/defaults and dependency locks; worker verifies the exact distribution/manifest/entrypoint/fixture source, runs the custom transform through the ordered data pipeline, checks declared output port and expected value, and rechecks source provenance after execution. The worker package includes the helper and compatibility advertises the generic extensions.component_conformance capability.

Integrated registered dataset, loss and metric component tests into the CLI. Dataset fixtures validate bounded length and indexed samples; losses must return the expected finite scalar and backpropagate finite input gradients; metrics must return finite fixture-matching values. Entry-point and fixture source fingerprints and locked component references are checked before and after execution.

Added a registered Layer state_roundtrip capability check through component test. A fresh instance loads the extension-owned state_dict with strict=True and must reproduce the original forward output; source fingerprints and locked component references are checked before and after. The finite state budget rejects deep/large/non-finite state.

Added registered Trainer conformance through the real external-loop engine: finite event fixtures check steps/loss/metrics, a stop-file fixture checks cooperative stop, and timeout fixtures verify the runner-owned cooperative deadline at a finite step boundary. The deadline is exposed as timeout_requested/remaining_time_seconds, and reporting another step after ignoring false fails conformance. A blocking Python/CUDA call remains non-preemptible by this cooperative contract.

Formal train timeout now writes the run-scoped cooperative stop request, waits at most 10 seconds for a step boundary, and then force-terminates the worker if it does not exit. Integration proves an external-loop step is checkpointed before a WORKER_TIMEOUT report; successful graceful exit also kills remaining ordinary worker process-group children. This is CLI-owned deadline handling, not a Trainer-owned timeout declaration.

Deadline origin is captured when the worker starts, so model import/construction time consumes the same runtime timeout budget as the CLI watchdog. The watchdog remains responsible for terminating a blocked worker after its grace window.

Closed a Layer conformance gap: the selected entrypoint is fingerprinted before/after construction and checks, component references are revalidated before reporting success, conditional claims stay conditional, and an unsupported construct declaration fails as a capability contradiction.

Extended capability/source integrity checks to regular Layer batch factories and conditional state-roundtrip claims: entrypoint and explicit batch module source fingerprints are rechecked before reporting; conditional Layer/Trainer checks retain conditional state and expose observed fixture success separately.

remaining: A runner-owned cooperative deadline is verified at a finite reported step boundary. It cannot preempt a blocked Python/CUDA call or guarantee checkpoint completion before the CLI watchdog terminates that process.
Finite fixtures do not prove arbitrary-input behavior or provide OS-level isolation; Python extension code executes with the selected interpreter permissions.
Value-component fixtures test bounded dataset samples, finite loss plus gradients, and metric output; they do not prove arbitrary datasets or domain-level metric correctness.
